rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
V = Σf(x−x̄)²/N
SD = √V
CV = (SD/x̄)×100%

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ treat "Mean" as one blob → ✅ split into: mean, variance, standard deviation of a random variable.  ·  ❌ state the rule without its limit → ✅ note when it applies / stops applying.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Variance = Σ(f·x − x̄)²/N (population) or /(N−1) (sample). SD = √Variance.  ·  Coefficient of Variation CV = (SD/mean)×100% (unit-free; compare different data sets).

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: μ = Σxi pi; Var = Σxi² pi − μ² — compute three columns (xipi, xi²pi) and subtract; never average the raw x values.  ·  Trick 2: SD = √Var — leave as a surd unless the square is exact; quoting Var when SD is asked loses the mark.

SD = √Variance.  ·  **Fact.** Coefficient of Variation CV = (SD/mean)×100% (unit-free; compare different data sets).  ·  **Fact.** Karl Pearson skewness = (mean − mode)/SD (3rd). Range and IQR as rough dispersion measures.

rows.text: Trick 3: Sanity bounds: μ must lie between min and max xi; Var ≥ 0 — use to catch arithmetic slips.  ·  Trick 4: For linear transforms Y = aX + b: μY = aμX + b, VarY = a²VarX — the shift b does NOT change variance.  ·  define + example each sub-idea: mean, variance, standard deviation of a random variable.
